issues.display_title: Issue #26: Update Save Validation & Prevent Email Spam (Profile, Location, Portfolio, Gear)
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Currently, the system triggers an email notification to support on every single "Save" action, regardless of the photographer's current status (Approved, Pending, or Denied). This causes severe inbox spam when a user clicks save multiple times.

We need to update the validation API on the backend to introduce a new moderation workflow and fix the email notification logic simultaneously.

New Business Logic

If a photographer with an "Approved" status makes updates to their data in any of the following sections and clicks save, their overall status must automatically revert to "Pending" (requiring re-moderation):

  • Profile
  • Location
  • Portfolio
  • Gear / Tools

Clarification (2026-06-11)

Email notifications to support are sent only for photographers who are in "Approved" status at the time of the save — and that save immediately flips their status to "Pending." Photographers already in pending or denied never generate an email, no matter how many times they save.

The email is dispatched directly from whichever of these 4 sections the user changed, and its content depends on what the user changed:

  • Profile
  • Location
  • Portfolio
  • Gear / Tools

In other words: the trigger is the Approved → Pending transition, the email originates at the edited section, and the email reflects the specific section(s) that changed.

Sub-tasks (Backend)

  1. Update Status Validation Logic: Modify the update/save API endpoints associated with the Profile, Location, Portfolio, and Gear/Tools modules. Add a condition checking the user's current status. If status == 'approved', update the user's status to pending upon a successful save in any of these sections.
  2. Fix Email Trigger Logic: Remove the generic email dispatch tied to the "Save" button click across all those 4 sections.
  3. Implement State-Transition Emails: Send a support email only when an approved photographer's save flips them to pending (the Approved → Pending transition). The email is dispatched from the edited section (Profile / Location / Portfolio / Gear) and indicates which section(s) changed. Do not send for saves by photographers already in pending/denied.
  4. Block Redundant Emails: If a user is already in a pending or denied state and clicks "Save" multiple times in any section to update their data, the system MUST NOT send additional emails to support.

Relevant code (for the assignee)

Status enum (src/action/v1/photographers/updatePhotographerStatus.go): 1 = pending, 2 = denied, 3 = approved, 4 = featured. Reverting an approved photographer means setting status = 1.

Update/save endpoints to add the status-revert condition to:

  • Profile: src/action/v1/photographers/updatePhotographerProfile.go
  • Location: src/action/v1/photographers/updatePhotographerLocation.go
  • Portfolio: src/action/v1/portfolio/createPhotographerPortfolio.go, updatePhotographerPortfolio.go, deletePhotographerPortfolio.go, updatePortfolioOrder.go
  • Gear / Tools: src/action/v1/photographers/addPhotographerEquipment.go, removePhotographerEquipment.go

⚠️ Investigation note: a save-triggered email to support is not currently dispatched from any of these update actions in this repo (only applyPhotographer, contactPhotographer, sendEmailReview, updatePhotographerStatus, and maintenance call helpers.SendEmail). The "email on every Save" is therefore coming from upstream (e.g. the dashboard) or a planned NotifyPhotographerUpdate flow (see brainstorm/brainstorming-api.md). Confirm where the current dispatch lives before removing it (sub-task 2), and centralize the new state-transition email on the pending-entry transition (sub-task 3).

Acceptance criteria

  • Saving Profile / Location / Portfolio / Gear by an approved photographer reverts their status to pending.
  • A support email is sent only on the approved → pending transition, dispatched from the edited section and naming the section(s) that changed.
  • No email is sent on a save when the photographer is already pending or denied.
  • Repeated saves in any section do not generate additional support emails.
  • Relevant Redis caches (detail / dashboard / markers) invalidated on the status change.

RESULT

Implemented the approved->pending re-moderation rule (sub-tasks 1 & 4). Sub-tasks 2 & 3 (auto support email on the transition) intentionally not wired in — confirmed with reporter that auto-emailing on save risks spam; support notification stays manual via the existing POST /:gothruUserId/notify-update endpoint.

Changes (commit 666278f):

  • New src/action/v1/photographers/revertApprovedToPending.go: shared RevertApprovedToPendingOnSave(gothruUserId) helper. If photographer.Status == approved(3), sets status = pending(1) and invalidates detail/dashboard/list/markers Redis caches. No-op for pending(1)/denied(2) — repeated saves never re-trigger.
  • Wired into all 8 save paths: updatePhotographerProfile.go, updatePhotographerLocation.go, createPhotographerPortfolio.go, updatePhotographerPortfolio.go, deletePhotographerPortfolio.go, updatePortfolioOrder.go, addPhotographerEquipment.go, removePhotographerEquipment.go.
  • Removed the old buggy unconditional status = denied(2) set in updatePhotographerProfile.go and the unconditional email send in updatePhotographerLocation.go (both fired regardless of current status).
  • notifyPhotographerUpdate.go: added optional section field to NotifyUpdateRequest, surfaced in email payload as changed_section, so the manual notify-update call can indicate which section (Profile/Location/Portfolio/Gear) changed.

Build + full test suite pass.

issues.display_title: Issue #28: Fix Issue Sub Locations API Payload Missing City and State Data
issues.main_description_html:
Description

A data fetching issue was identified on the Backend API serving the Photographer Detail page.

When inspecting the "Sub Locations" modal on the frontend, the UI renders empty punctuation (,,) in the location column. Upon further investigation, the frontend is behaving this way because the backend payload for the sub_locations array is incomplete. The API is returning null or empty strings for specific regional data (like city or state/province), even though this data should be available for regions like Canada and the United States.

Root cause (confirmed in code)

The photographer detail action loads sublocations without preloading the City relation:

src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographerDetailBySlug.go:46-47

var sublocations []models.DirectoryPhotographerSublocation
config.GetConnPhotographers().Where("photographer_id = ?", phot.ID).Find(&sublocations)

The model declares a foreign-key relation that GORM only populates when explicitly preloaded:

src/models/directory_photographer_sublocation.go

CityID int            `gorm:"column:city_id;not null" json:"city_id"`
City   *DirectoryCity `gorm:"foreignKey:CityID" json:"city"`   // <-- never loaded -> serializes as null

Because there is no .Preload("City"), every sublocation in the response has "city": null, so the frontend has no city / state-province name to render and falls back to ,,.

Fix

Preload the City relation (and, if state/province display requires it, the city's country/region) when fetching sublocations:

config.GetConnPhotographers().
    Preload("City").
    Where("photographer_id = ?", phot.ID).
    Find(&sublocations)

Notes for the assignee:

  • DirectoryCity currently exposes Name + CountryID (src/models/...city...go). Confirm where state/province comes from — if it's a separate column/relation (e.g. a region or via country_id), preload/return that too so the frontend gets both city and state.
  • The same missing-preload pattern may exist on other sublocation read paths — grep for DirectoryPhotographerSublocation reads and verify each.
  • The detail response is Redis-cached (PhotographerDetail); bump/invalidate the cache so the corrected payload is served.

Acceptance criteria

  • sub_locations[*].city is populated (not null) in the photographer detail payload when city_id resolves to a city.
  • City and state/province (and country, if shown) are present so the frontend location column renders correctly for Canada and US regions — no more ,,.
  • Sublocations with a missing/invalid city_id degrade gracefully (no 500).
  • Detail Redis cache invalidated so existing cached entries don't keep serving the incomplete payload.
  • Verified against the photographer in the report (Toronto, Canada — sublocations "Canada" / "United States").

RESULT

Confirmed root cause via direct DB check (read-only, joining photographer_sublocations -> city -> state/country): city.state_id is well-populated (e.g. Toronto sublocations resolve to Saskatchewan/Canada, Colorado/United States), but was never exposed by the model or query.

Changes (commit aeee603):

  • src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographerDetailBySlug.go: sublocations query now does Preload("City.State").Preload("City.Country"), so sub_locations[*].city is populated with name, state, and country instead of null.
  • src/models/directory_city.go: added StateID/State *DirectoryState (foreign key city.state_id).
  • src/models/directory_state.go: this model previously mapped to a non-existent states table with mismatched columns (dead code, unused anywhere). Rewrote it to map to the real state table (id, name, country_id, state_code, type, latitude, longitude) and wired it into DirectoryCity.

Other DirectoryPhotographerSublocation read paths checked: getPhotographerLocation.go returns a flat SublocationInfo DTO that doesn't expose city/state at all (out of scope here); addSublocation/updateSublocation/removeSublocation already invalidate the detail cache on write.

Cache: existing PhotographerDetail Redis entries were cached before this fix and will keep serving the old (incomplete) payload until they expire (24h TTL) or are flushed manually — no code-level cache-version bump done since that constant is shared across many unrelated cache keys.

Build + existing test suite pass.

UPDATE

Follow-up commit c79fa1c: aligned sub_locations[*] shape with the old Node.js getPhotographersDetailBySlug response — now a flat object {id, name, addressLine1, addressLine2, cityId, cityName, country, continent, latitude, longitude} instead of raw model serialization. Dropped the city.state/DirectoryState model addition from the previous commit since the old Node response never exposed state/province (State confirmed unused).

RESULT

issues.display_title: Issue #29: Fix Issue Can't Delete Sub Location
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 11/06/26

✅ Implementation Complete — Ready for Unit Testing

Commit : https://github.com/GoThruMedia/gothru-maps-backend-go/commit/8abb560565c22c6b8846d78bca8284441b7e9557

Implementation :

Report

A photographer (Werner Getzmann) reports he can't edit or delete his branch (sub) locations.

  • gothru user id: 253
  • photographer username/slug: clever-click
  • Route: DELETE https://apil.gothru.co/photographers/profile/delete-sub-location/36
  • Status Code: 409 Conflict
  • Response body: 
    { "statusCode": 404, "data": { "messages": "Failed to delete sub-location" } }

🔒 The user's JWT was included in the report — omitted here on purpose (don't paste live auth tokens into issues). If it was shared anywhere public, it should be rotated/revoked.

Investigation notes (grounded in this repo)

1. The failing request is hitting the LEGACY API, not this Go service.

  • Reported path: /photographers/profile/delete-sub-location/36 on host apil.gothru.co.
  • This Go service's delete route is different: DELETE /v1/photographers/:identifier/sublocations/:sublocationId (src/routes/v1/photographersRoutes.go:54).
  • The reported response shape { "statusCode", "data": { "messages" } } is the legacy Node format. This Go service returns { "error": ... } via helpers.FormatResponse and never returns 409 (only 400 / 404 / 500 — see src/controllers/v1/sublocation/removeSublocation.go).
  • So first question for the assignee: is the dashboard still calling the legacy endpoint, and should it be migrated to the Go endpoint? Or is this a legacy-side bug? Confirm which backend owns delete-sublocation in production.

2. Likely cause in the Go delete path (if/when migrated). RemoveSublocation (src/action/v1/sublocations/removeSublocation.go) deletes only when the row matches both id and owner:

db.Where("id = ? AND photographer_id = ?", sublocationID, photographer.ID).First(&sublocation) // -> ErrSublocationNotFound (404) if no match

The photographer is resolved from the :identifier (numeric → gothru_user_id, else → slug). If the dashboard passes an identifier that resolves to a photographer whose id ≠ the sublocation's photographer_id, this returns 404 "sublocation not found" — a plausible match for the reported 404 body. Verify that sublocation 36 actually belongs to the photographer with gothru_user_id = 253 / slug clever-click.

3. The 409 Conflict (HTTP) is suspicious. A 409 at the HTTP layer (despite a 404 in the JSON body) typically indicates a database foreign-key constraint blocking the delete — i.e. other rows still reference photographer_sublocations.id = 36. Check for FK constraints / dependent rows before deleting, and delete/cascade them or return a clear error. (This 409 is almost certainly legacy-side, reinforcing note 1.)

Acceptance criteria

  • Confirm which backend serves delete-sublocation in production (legacy apil.gothru.co vs this Go service) and document it; if the dashboard should use the Go endpoint, track the migration.
  • Deleting sublocation 36 for gothru_user_id 253 / clever-click succeeds (or returns an accurate, actionable error if the row genuinely doesn't belong to that user).
  • If a FK/related-row constraint blocks deletion, it is handled (cascade or explicit, correct error) — no misleading 409 Conflict + 404 body mismatch.
  • Verify edit of sublocations as well (the user reports both edit and delete failing) — see updateSublocation.go.
  • Detail / markers / geodata Redis caches invalidated after a successful delete (the Go action already does this — confirm it runs).
